newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria central bank cuts monthly rate to 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria central bank cuts monthly rate to 15 pct.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) cut the monthly interest rate to 15 percent from the current 20 percent, effective November 4, the BNB said in a statement.

"The cut is supported by a reduction in consumer price inflation over the past two weeks and an increase in the foreign exchange reserves of the BNB this month compared to September," said the statement.

Foreign exchange reserves stood at $506 million last month. The BNB has not yet announced this month's level of forex reserves, but it has been seen buying hard currency on the local interbank market in the past weeks.
BNB officials were not immediately available for comment.
The BNB hiked the central interest rate on September 23 to an all-time high of 300 percent in a bid to stabilise the crumbling lev and financial system, saying that the measure was temporary.
The annual rate was reduced to 240 percent or a monthly 20 percent two weeks ago. The new annual rate which comes into effect on Monday will be 180 percent.
The rate cut coincides with a visit of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission in Sofia to review reform progress and map a draft budget frame for next year.

Bulgaria has topped its revised macroeconomic targets which had envisaged an annual central interest rate of 65 percent and annual inflation of 105 percent, considerably below the current cumulative figure of 153 percent.

The BNB has been under heavy pressure from the socialist government to ease credit because the high rates are stifling the country's stagnant economy and have made domestic debt payments unaffordably high.
Economy Minister Roumen Gechev said recently that it was impossible to plan a budget for next year under current interest rates.
